<main>
    <h1>Projective texture mapping</h1>
    <p class="lede">A slide projector is a camera that shines its picture instead of recording one. Each vertex goes through the light's view and projection matrices and a bias, which gives the <code>(s, t, depth, q)</code> coordinate that <code>textureProj</code> divides by <code>q</code>. This page extends <code>projectiveTexture</code> with a choice of textures, colour, a floor and several objects to catch the slide, and shadows from a depth map rendered from the same projector.</p>

    <div id="fatal" class="fatal" hidden></div>

    <section class="notes">
        <h2>What this page changes from projectiveTexture.js</h2>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>The projection.</strong> The original computes <code>0.5*clip.xyz + 0.5</code> and hands it to <code>textureProj</code>, which divides by the third component, not by <code>w</code>. Here the vertex shader computes <code>Bias * P_light * V_light * Model * position</code> and <code>textureProj</code> divides by <code>q = w</code>. Points behind the projector have <code>q &lt; 0</code> and are switched off; otherwise they would receive a mirrored copy of the slide.</li>
            <li><strong>The projector's position.</strong> The original puts the projector at <code>normalize(lightPosition)</code>, 1 unit from the origin, while its facing test uses the light's real position. Here one position is used for both.</li>
            <li><strong>The sampler.</strong> The original sets <code>uTexture</code> but the shader reads <code>uTextureMap</code>; it works only because unit 0 is the default. Here both names agree.</li>
            <li><strong>Shadows</strong> use a <code>DEPTH_COMPONENT24</code> texture and a <code>sampler2DShadow</code>, with the same texture coordinate as the slide: the shadow map is itself a projective texture.</li>
            <li><strong>rotateY.</strong> The page uses <code>rotate(angle, vec3(0, 1, 0))</code> rather than <code>rotateY</code>, as the light-view explorer does.</li>
        </ul>
    </section>
